title: First records with Charlie Creath and Dewey Jackson; segregation on the St. Louis boat
summary: Foster says he was on the Creath records, and recalls guards at the bandstand in St. Louis.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: I was going to ask about your very first records. Were you on an old record that Fate Marable made with Sidney Dez Bean and Amos White? No.
You weren't on that? I was on that.
Which were your first records? Were you on the Charlie Crust?

Yeah, I was on the Charlie Crust with Dewey Jackson. We made records so safe then, Amos White. See, I was on the boat long for them guys. Amos White. Them guys come on the boat way late. When we first went to St. Louis, the white around St. Louis didn't think Cullors could play no music. That's how bad it was on St. Louis. We had guards, the gardeners around that music stand for the whole summer we was up there.
I heard Baby and all of them talking about it too.

We didn't know it. We just thought the guys would stand around the stand. We didn't know it. We didn't know nothing to laugh. We hear it's laughter. You don't put enough whiskey in it. We're not supposed to have a song. That's going on there, man. You don't put enough whiskey in it. That's going on there. That's going on there. That's going on there. That's not right. That's the sport to have it weak anyway then. Oh, that's all right. I didn't think of anything else to ask you really, Pops. I mean, it's wonderful all the things you've told us already.
